subject: Daz

subject: The Narrator

subject: Rope (used with Street Justice)

It extends battlefield dominance beyond the initial action, allowing him to pin enemies while freeing himself to act elsewhere — a critical adaptation in tight Underdark environments.
source_quote: The monk whose hands were already his primary weapon, now with a formal mechanism for making staying as interesting as hitting.

source_quote: The spellbook we'd taken from Princess Ebonmire had been sitting in my pack like a promissory note I hadn't finished reading.

subject: Conservation of Action
fact: Conservation of Action is the discipline of using bonus actions, free castings, and multi-step sequences to maximize control per turn in high-stakes combat.
source_quote: Grapple is a quick thing — one motion... The binding would consume the action itself. The whole turn — both pieces of it — spent on one enemy...

subject: Dark Transition
fact: Dark Transition is the irreversible shift from idealistic adventurer to pragmatic survivor who adopts morally compromised tactics for survival.
source_quote: I've had what you might call a dark transition. The happy-go-lucky kid who went underground expecting something survivable has spent months watching demon lords and eating mushrooms and coming to understand that the Underdark doesn't care what kind of person you want to be.

subject: Divine Radiance as Philosophy
fact: Divine Radiance as Philosophy is the idea that radiant damage is not merely a damage type but a metaphysical assertion against darkness, requiring belief as much as spellcasting.
source_quote: The blade doesn't cut so much as it burns — clean, divine, the kind of light that argues with darkness on a philosophical level.

subject: feats evaluation
fact: Daz and Zalthir are both in the midst of a deep, unspoken evaluation of feats, with implications for their tactical roles and synergies, leaving the final decisions unresolved and open to future refinement.
source_quote: I went back to my own list.

subject: Geometry Over Power
fact: Geometry Over Power is the principle that precise spatial control — grapples, repositioning, area effect sculpting — defeats brute force in the Underdark’s confined spaces.
source_quote: The Evoker's toolkit is not a collection of separate spells; it is an interlocking argument about where enemies should be, where allies should be, and which parts of a room I am willing to set on fire.

subject: identity of the Ember entities
fact: It is unresolved whether the Ember Vanguard and the Ember Grapple are the same party described from two different positions — a foreshadowed ambiguity in factional identity.
source_quote: Both accurate. Possibly the same party described from two different positions in the room.

subject: lack of ranged capability
fact: The party has no ranged weapons or abilities, creating a critical vulnerability that will inevitably be exploited when facing flying or distant enemies — a flaw the Narrator recognizes as a looming, inevitable failure point in their survival strategy.
source_quote: Not having anyone who can reach a flying enemy is going to come back and bite us.

subject: Lack of Ranged Capability
fact: The party has no reliable ranged attackers, a critical vulnerability that will inevitably lead to tactical failure when facing flying or distant enemies. This gap is acknowledged as a looming threat — not a flaw to be fixed, but a reality to be compensated for through positioning and control.
source_quote: Which is also why not having anyone who can reach a flying enemy is going to come back and bite us.

subject: Legacy of Giants
fact: Legacy of Giants is the inherited combat doctrine that protection, proximity, and brute force replace ranged capability, rooted in the training of hill giants.
source_quote: Being a dwarf raised by giants means I don't have to have any range. Giants toss rocks. Those rocks go far and hurt. My job was to be there and protect the giants from anything that came too close.

subject: My potion-saving habit
fact: I have a bad habit of saving potions for later, and I recognize it as one more habit to account for.
source_quote: Which — I recognized, even as I thought it — had given me one more bad habit to account for.

subject: Our lack of ranged weapons
fact: We have no ranged weapons, and this will come back and bite us in a dangerous world where distance matters.
source_quote: The Underdark is tight and low. But we're almost out. And this is a dangerous world, and we have a dangerous job, and we none of us have ranged weapons, which means there will absolutely be something that needs hitting from a distance. The universe is that kind of petty.

subject: Potion Hoarding
fact: Potion Hoarding is the bad habit of saving potent resources for a future that may never come, leading to death with unspent power.
source_quote: The potion you don't drink is the potion you die holding.

subject: Sculpting the Battlefield
fact: Sculpting the Battlefield is the art of using spells not to destroy, but to define safe and lethal zones, turning the environment into a weapon.
source_quote: Sculpt Spells lets me carve exclusions into area effects... The Evoker's toolkit is not a collection of separate spells; it is an interlocking argument about where enemies should be, where allies should be...

subject: Tactical Geometry
fact: Tactical geometry is the recurring theme that battles are won by positioning, not power, and that control over space matters more than raw damage.
source_quote: The Underdark had taught me repeatedly that battles are often decided by who is standing where... Zalthir builds narrow and builds sharp. Everything pointing in one direction, so that in exactly the right situation, he becomes something close to impossible.

subject: The Dark Transition
fact: The Narrator is undergoing a profound moral and tactical transformation — from an idealistic adventurer to a hardened pragmatist shaped by the Underdark’s cruelty. This transition is not yet complete, but its direction is clear: he is becoming someone who no longer apologizes for the darkness he has absorbed.
source_quote: There are things you absorb down here whether you mean to or not.

subject: The Ember Grapple
fact: The Ember Grapple is a name that has been accepted, though its origin or exact referent remains ambiguous.
source_quote: I let it settle. As names go, I have heard worse.

subject: The Ember Grapple
fact: The Ember Grapple may describe the same party as the Ember Vanguard, but from a different position in the room — this is not confirmed.
source_quote: Both accurate. Possibly the same party described from two different positions in the room.

subject: the Ember Grapple
fact: The name 'The Ember Grapple' has been adopted by the group as a functional descriptor of Zalthir and Daz’s synergy — not one Zalthir originally claimed, but one he accepts as accurate, marking a quiet transformation from lone warrior to tactical anchor.
source_quote: I did not correct it. The name was not wrong.

subject: The Long Arrangement
fact: The Long Arrangement is the philosophy that preparation, positioning, and spell selection are the truest parts of combat, not the moment of casting.
source_quote: Milo Goodbarrel had a chapter about this. He called it "the long arrangement" — the idea that the fight before the fight, the positioning, the preparation, is actually most of the fight.

subject: The Weight of Choice
fact: The Weight of Choice is the burden of knowing that every feat, spell, and tactic chosen is not just mechanical, but existential — it defines who you become.
source_quote: I knew it was wrong when I said it. It's always wrong... I could. It would be honest, even. Not the honesty I prefer — I've always liked honesty you can stand behind without flinching — but there are things you absorb down here whether you mean to or not.
